state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's revisit the concept of range in this context. Remember, the range is the difference between the highest and lowest values in a set of data. Think about how cutting all the plant heights in half or adding the same amount to each height would affect the overall range. Can you explain your reasoning for why you agree with Tom?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I thought that if you cut all the heights in half, the highest and lowest would still be in the same proportion, so the range wouldn't change. But now I'm not sure if that's right. Can you explain how adding \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) would change the range?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's consider how adding \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) to each plant height would affect the range. Remember, the range is the difference between the highest and lowest values. Think about how increasing each height by the same amount would impact the overall range. Can you describe your thought process as you work through this scenario?
